text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Supporters turned out in thousands to attend the launching of the opposition Socialist Party campaign for the mayorship of Tirana. Another rally took place normally in Shkoder where they had not been allowed in in the past.

- Vehbi Alimuca, the president and owner of Vefa, the country's biggest company, said they plan to invest $600 million next year and lower the interest of the loans they receive from single creditors in the future.
- If raw materials for chicken feed were produced in Albania, the price of eggs could be seven leks per piece rather than the current 13 leks.

- The Italian ambassador to Albania, Paolo Foresti, said Italian investors encounter difficulties in Albania, especially with the customs and fiscal systems. He blamed the problems on the mentality of Albanian officials.
- More than 700 Albanian officers will be trained in modern military techniques based on the German model.
- A man was sentenced to one year in jail for forcing a young girl to work as prostitute in Italy. The prosecutor had demanded a 15-year jail term.

- Bashkim Kopliku, a senior leader of the ruling Democratic Party and former deputy prime minister, initiated legal proceedings against Koha Jone after it published stories his contested plans to extend his apartment.
- A man wounded in a shoot-out between rival gangs a month ago has died, bringing to two the number of fatalities from that incident.
- People up to the age of 50 will be vaccinated against a polio virus from October 7 in a large-scale operation which will involve helicopters to reach outlying areas.
- Trade unions asking for wage rises to compensate for higher bread prices will hold a 24-hour strike in education, health, transport and other services sectors.
- An Italian customs agent admitted in court that he had been the kingpin in an operation to forge documents of goods entering Albania from Italy's Otranto port.
